acceptance: Preserve all caller constraints;candidate self-tests and printed timing never replace independent correctness or performance acceptance.

investigate: Read the entry point and relevant callers through code memory;write down mathematical operation,shape domain,dtype,independent input/output strides,aliasing and error policy.
Identify allowed backend,hardware and build environment. Locate independent reference/tests before choosing tiling or fusion.
implement: Decompose into compute primitives and explicit address mappings for every buffer;prove complete input/output coverage,unique writers and required synchronization.
Implement the simplest correct permitted path first;preserve the verified baseline before testing optimization candidates.
diagnose: Use the independent failure's case,location and error type;trace values and addresses with use-def/call/structure views. Separate build,layout,numerical,coverage and synchronization failures.
State one falsifiable cause and make a focused source change;re-run the failed case and then all independent correctness checks. Do not weaken valid input requirements.
validate: Run caller-owned correctness checks on the current source;include tails,empty/degenerate domains,non-contiguous layouts,precision and alias cases when allowed by the contract.

After correctness,measure warm latency distribution,throughput and peak memory on fixed hardware;change one bottleneck hypothesis,then recheck correctness and retain or revert based on independent measurements.

reduction: Specify identity,participating elements,tie/NaN policy and accumulation precision;trace each input contribution and initialize every consumed partial.
contraction: Separate logical contraction axes from physical layouts;check partial tiles,reuse scope,accumulation type and fusion dependencies before choosing a schedule.
